subject: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility + next steps (HealthCloud)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility + next steps (HealthCloud)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap:
- HealthCloud confirmed you process PHI for patient messaging and scheduling (patient names, dates of birth, limited medical notes).
- Main ask: confirm whether Redwood can sign a BAA and which deployment modes are eligible for PHI.
- You also requested our SOC 2 report and that we start the vendor security questionnaire.

Redwood summary (high level):
- BAA: we can sign a BAA for customers handling PHI, but the deployment mode matters.
- Eligible deployment modes for PHI: Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC or on-prem).
- Hosted API (our shared, public hosted tier) is not available for PHI workloads under our standard terms.
- Controls available: customer KMS integration, request-level audit logs, option to disable training/retention of prompts, and encryption at rest/in transit.

Attachments I'm sharing now: Redwood_BAA_Draft.pdf (redacted template) and SOC2_2025_Redacted.pdf. Also attaching our HIPAA_Deployment_Matrix.xlsx which outlines feature differences across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Jordan / Aisha: please send over the HealthCloud vendor security questionnaire (VSA) and any specific BAA clauses you require.
2) Redwood (Neha + Vivek): we will review the questionnaire and confirm any clarifications; Neha will confirm the SOC 2 scope and controls mapping; Vivek will confirm any legal/contract notes on the BAA.
3) Aim to get a completed questionnaire back within 5 business days and a draft BAA turnaround in 7-10 business days.

If this looks right, I'll loop in Legal for the BAA signature path and schedule a 30-minute follow-up with your security team next week.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 07:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility + next steps (HealthCloud)

Thanks Marissa / Jordan. Quick security/legal notes for the thread so Marissa can summarize back to HealthCloud: 

SOC 2 / Compliance:
- We have a SOC 2 Type II report (audit period ended 2025-12-31). The redacted PDF is attached (SOC2_2025_Redacted.pdf). We can produce a fully redacted version for vendor review; unredacted reports require an NDA.

BAA and deployment modes:
- Redwood can sign a BAA for customers processing PHI. Our supported deployment options for PHI are: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC peering or on-prem appliance).
- Hosted (shared) API is not permitted for PHI in our standard offering. If a customer requires hosted with PHI, that requires a custom procurement/legal exception and additional controls (rare; handled on a case-by-case basis).

PHI handling boundaries / controls:
- Data in flight is TLS-protected; at rest we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- We offer options to disable prompt retention and disable model telemetry for PHI workloads (we document these in the HIPAA_Deployment_Matrix.xlsx).
- Audit logs and per-request metadata are available for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps we need from HealthCloud:
1) Completed vendor security questionnaire (we received a copy from Jordan).
2) Data flow diagram (how PHI will flow into/out of Redwood services).
3) Confirmation of preferred deployment (Dedicated or Private) and any residency requirements.

I'll take point on mapping the VSA responses to our controls (SOC 2 sections, encryption, access controls). Marissa — once you have the VSA back, I’ll schedule a short walkthrough with their security team if needed.

-Neha
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
